Hon'ble Shri Justice Narendra Kumar Vyas Order on Board 20/07/2023
1.

These are the first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, for grant of anticipatory bail, who have apprehension of being arrested in connection with Crime No. 197/2023, registered at Police Station- Katghora, District- Korba (C.G.)
for the offence punishable under Sections 420, 457, 380, 406, 411, 34 of I.P.C.
2.

Case of the prosecution, in brief, is that the complainant Gourav Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:18178 Modi lodged a written complaint to Superintendent of Police, Korba on 14.01.2020 referring to complaint dated 10.01.2020 to T.I. Katghora alleging that one Munir Ahmad Avinash Murarka vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152817558/
1 has committed theft of motor parts in the year 2020, but no action has been taken by the prosecution.

entities.text: Munir Ahmad Avinash Murarka vs State Of Chhattisgarh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thereafter, an application under Section 156(3) of the Cr.P.C. before Judicial Magistrate First Class was filed by the complainant alleging that complainant runs a firm namely Krishna & company and deals in motor spare parts and co- accused namely Munir Ahmad was manager in his firm.

In January, 2020, spare parts were found shortage, on being enquired, Munir Ahmed disclosed that he used to sell the spare parts to the applicant in MCRCA No.
694/2023-Avinash Murarka who is owner of Tirupati Motor Champa & applicant in MCRCA No.
883/2023- Devendra Kumar Dewangan, who is an employee of Avinash Murarka.

On the basis of the application filed under Section 156 (3) Cr.P.C., the Judicial Magistrate First Class directed for registration of FIR against applicant, therefore, offence afore-stated has been registered against both the applicants.
3. Learned counsel for the applicants would submit that the applicants are innocent and have been falsely implicated in the crime in question.

They would further submit that the registration of FIR is in violation of law laid down by Hon'ble the Supreme Court in Lalita Kumari Vs. Uttar Pradesh &
others reported in (2014) 2 SCC 1.

entities.text:
Lalita Kumari Vs. Uttar Pradesh &
others reported in (2014) 2 SCC 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: They would further submit that more than 200 staff members were appointed under applicant's firm and false complaint has been made by the complainant because of business rivalry.
They would further submit that there is manipulation on the inventory and on that basis calculation of theft has been taken to the tune of Rs. 21,35,000/-.

They would further submit that during pendency of the bail applications, the applicant in MCRCA No.
694/2023-Avinash Murarka has already returned amount of Rs. 20,25,970/- to the complainant.
Hence, it is prayed that the applicants should be granted anticipatory bail.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State opposing the Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:18178 anticipatory bail application submits that there is clear allegation against the applicants regarding commission of offence.
Hence, it is prayed that the application for grant of anticipatory bail may be rejected.

5. Learned counsel for the complainant would submit that amount of Rs. 20,25,970/- has been returned by the applicant- Avinash Murarka to the complainant, but the amount of GST has not been given to the complainant.
Hence, it is prayed that the applications for grant of anticipatory bail may be rejected.
6. Heard learned counsel for both the parties and perused the case diary.

7. Considering the fact and circumstances of the case and also considering the fact that the applicant- Avinash Murarka has already returned amount of Rs. 20,25,970/- to the complainant, I am inclined to extend the benefit of Section 438 of the Cr.P.C. to both the applicants.

8. Accordingly, the instant anticipatory bail applications are allowed and It is directed that in the event of arrest of the applicants in connection with the aforesaid offence, they shall be released on anticipatory bail by the officer arresting them on each of them executing a personal bond in sum of Rs. 25,000/- with one surety each in the like sum to the satisfaction of the concerned Investigating Officer.
